query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a Ti interlayer between W and Cu can overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, improving thermal conductivity.
generation.material_initial_state: W-Cu composite with W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix
generation.conditions: Heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components
generation.mechanism: Improved wettability and bonding between W and Cu due to the Ti interlayer, reducing interfacial voids and enhancing thermal conductivity
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite
generation.boundary: Processing conditions: temperature, pressure, and duration of Ti interlayer introduction; Service conditions: temperature, irradiation dose, and duration
generation.uncertainty: Optimal thickness and microstructure of the Ti interlayer, potential effects of irradiation on the Ti interlayer

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of thermal conductivity between W-Cu composites with and without a Ti interlayer, under relevant heat-transfer and irradiation conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal conductivity of the W-Cu composite with a Ti interlayer is not significantly higher than that of the untreated composite, the hypothesis is falsified.
